title: Time to onset of clinically relevant hyponatremia under treatment with oxcarbazepine
summary: Oxcarbazepine (OXC) is a commonly used medication for epilepsy. However, it can lead to a dangerous sodium deficiency in the blood (hyponatremia) in some patients, especially in older individuals. Since this can have serious consequences, we want to find out in a study when, after starting OXC, the risk of such a sodium deficiency is highest. This will help determine the best time for blood tests to monitor sodium levels.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients who developed hyponatremia during oxcarbazepine therapy between 2020 and 2025

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Initiation of oxcarbazepine treatment under inpatient conditions.
Normal serum sodium concentration of at least 135 mmol/L prior to initiation of oxcarbazepine treatment.
Exclusion criteria:
Concomitant medication with drugs that could potentially lower serum sodium.
Additional medical conditions that could affect serum sodium, e.g., syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH).
